svg.text: How we got here: Prochlorococcus amino-acid pathways, 2026-11-04
Each card = one step of the session: the question that started it, how it was done (KG tools), what it produced, and what it showed.
Side notes = gaps, choices and corrections found along the way. Commit ids = local git history of analyses/2026-11-04-prochlorococcus_aa_pathways.
All KG data on Prochlorococcus amino-acid biosynthesis and degradation: genes per pathway, and under which
conditions they go up or down.
How: Loaded the research-methodology rules · kg_release_info
How: genes_by_ontology: 14 KEGG amino-acid pathways + 40 GO 'biosynthetic / catabolic process' terms
→ Median 2 (Trp metabolism) to 24 genes per pathway; GO catabolic terms nearly empty
PAC1 skipped: its name also matches EQPAC1
Under which conditions are these genes up / down?
→ 8,241 rows, 67 experiments; every pathway changes under most conditions; whole-genome change 1–88%
Draw the pathways and how they meet the TCA cycle, with strain counts.
How: Step list from textbook biochemistry (59 arrows, 120 genes as KEGG KOs) · KO presence via API (44) + Cypher (PAC1),
cross-checked identical (4,541 rows) · genes_by_function name search in MED4
→ TCA open: sucA/B 0/45, sucC/D 0/45 · His 0/45 only because hisN is unannotated · degradation mostly 0/45
psp); PSTA has a wrong KO → counted by
How: Genes behind the KEGG 'degradation' pathways
→ Mostly shared enzymes (ALDH, lpd, transaminases); real ones few: hdc 43/44, DAO 42/44
My map missed hdc, DAO, leucine DH, mmsB
Do papers discuss the open TCA cycle or the His gap?
How: list_publications · discussed_by_publication over all 60 papers
→ No paper discusses either; closest: Tolonen 2006 — acnB/icd 'synthesis of 2-oxoglutarate', up under N stress
Which strains have which genes, and which pathways are incomplete?
How: 151 gene rows (path order) × 45 strains, Jaccard + average-linkage clustering
→ 18 of 20 amino acids complete in 41–45 genomes; gaps sit in 6 strains (HNLC2 11, HNLC1 7, MIT9313 4 …); Asn
HNLC genomes may be incomplete assemblies —
Which genes change, under which conditions?
How: Fresh DE pull for every map locus tag · 101 genes × 67 experiments, any timepoint, any paralog
→ Nitrogen and darkness columns densest; iron / viral / phosphorus near-blank (partial tables)
Three maps: nitrogen, extended light/darkness, mitomycin.
How: 13 experiments chosen in chat · one square per gene per experiment
→ N: protein leans up (56/19), coculture RNA down (14/35) · NATL2A darkness leans down
Experiment lists are my choice — to confirm
Which routes can run forward, backward, or both?
How: Per-step reversibility from textbook biochemistry (not KG)
→ 5 of 24 biosynthesis arrows run both ways (Asp, Ala, Val, Gly, homoserine); 12 of 18 exits have no gene
Patterns and gaps; explain 'carbon meets nitrogen at 2-OG'.
How: Synthesis of all files · cell illustration
→ Build everything, break down almost nothing; open TCA ends at 2-OG, which GS-GOGAT uses to take up NH₄⁺
Show the calculation, step by step.
How: Standalone script, fresh KG queries, independent code; compares every square with the saved file
double count) · darkness lean is NATL2A only;
extended light also leans down · constant-dark
has 94/97 genes not in table · 'both' was left
Is each claim actually in the KG?
How: metabolites_by_gene (reactions) · genes_by_metabolite (L-glutamate) · assays_by_metabolite (2-OG) · DE incl. ntcA
→ Reactions verified (glnA R00253, GOGAT R00021, icd R00267); 14/20 amino acids get N via Glu/Gln/NH₄⁺; glnA and
Not in KG: carbon flux to 2-OG · 2-OG build-up
• Supported by the KG: biosynthesis genes for 18/20 amino acids in 41–45 genomes; open TCA as annotated; GS-GOGAT and transaminase reactions; glnA and ntcA induced under N stress.
• Not yet in hand: carbon flux, 2-OG under N stress, hisN identity, a TCA bypass, HNLC genome completeness, any test against the genome-wide background.
• Status: Plan-phase data collection only — no proposal.md, no statistics, no critic review yet. Next: confirm experiment sets, then enrichment per condition / bypass and hisN search.
